title: Speak Out! Support Affordable Housing! Attend County Commission Hearing
description:
On Wednesday, June 18 at 10:00 am (all attendees are urged to get there by 9:00), the Hillsborough Board of County Commissioners (BOCC) will hold a public hearing on whether to repeal the HOPE Affordable Housing Act. The Republican-majority BOCC is chomping at the bit to do away with this fund--a potential lifeline for many families in Hillsborough County who struggle to afford the greatly increasing costs of housing. 

Here’s how YOU CAN HELP! 
Help us stop the Republican County Commissioners from eliminating this lifeline, by joining your fellow North Tampa Dems and other concerned citizens in showing up to the hearing and making our presence known.  

Need inspiration? Get it from one of our active members, Tom Cobert, who took a stand for HOPE in front of the BOCC last Wednesday when they met to discuss the fate of this essential initiative. 

Tom points out that the Commissioners "are forgetting their constituents are some of these needy poor people...There are voters watching this."

Join fellow Democrats and like-minded citizens in defending the HOPE Affordable Housing Act. Let our County Commissioners know that they work for ALL of Hillsborough County--including the most vulnerable among us. We understand that News Channel 8 will be there. 

Please wear your North Tampa Dems T-shirt or any other Democratic T-shirt, to show the commission that Democrats are watching and listening! Let’s do the most Democratic thing we can do—fight for those who can’t fight for themselves. 

Details below:
Location: County Center at 601 E. Kennedy Blvd
Time: Meeting starts at 10:00, but we urge you to show up by 9:00 am. If you sign up to speak, you must sign-in by 9:00 am.

title: Sign the Petition for SB1 Referendum in Delphos

## WHAT IS SENATE BILL 1?

- Senate Bill 1  (“The Higher Education Destruction Act”) was signed into OH law by Gov. DeWine on March 28, 2025 and goes into effect on June 25, 2025. 
- SB1 guts collective bargaining rights for faculty unions, removes job protections for educators & bans striking time for full-time staff.
- SB1 allows colleges & universities to end programs & terminate faculty positions without warning or cause.
- SB1 bans most diversity, equity & inclusion programs and staff training in higher education.
- We have until June 22 to collect 250,000 signatures in OH and get a repeal measure on the Nov. ballot.
- Republicans in OH leadership have now introduced bills (SB113 & HB155) targeted at grades K-12. We must stop attacks on public education!
- For more information, visit [ohiosb1petition.com](ohiosb1petition.com)
- Sign the petition to repeal SB1!

title: Indivisible Sonoma County - Truth in Media Film Series: Z
description:
Indivisible Sonoma County, in conjunction with Rialto Cinemas Sebastopol, continues our monthly Truth in Media Film Series. A portion of the proceeds is donated to Indivisible Sonoma County.

This month: Costa-Gavra's Z.

**Two screenings 1pm and 7pm. Panel discussion with Stephen F. Rohde and Dr. Marco Calavita to follow 7 pm screening!**

A pulse-pounding political thriller, the Greek expatriate director's Z was one of the cinematic sensations of the late sixties, and remains among the most vital dispatches from that hallowed era of filmmaking. 

This Academy Award winner—loosely based on the 1963 assassination of Greek left-wing activist Gregoris Lambrakis—stars Yves Montand as a prominent politician and doctor whose public murder amid a violent demonstration is covered up by military and government officials; Jean-Louis Trintignant is the tenacious magistrate who’s determined not to let them get away with it. 

Z is a technically audacious and emotionally gripping masterpiece featuring kinetic and rhythmic editing, Raoul Coutard’s expressive vérité photography, and Mikis Theodorakis’s unforgettable, propulsive score.

title: Canvass in Alpharetta - Debra Shigley for Georgia
description:
Join us to canvass in Alpharetta with Debra Shigley for State Senate! GA Senate District 21 runs through Cherokee and Fulton Counties and the seat is vacant, meaning we have the opportunity to elect a Democrat to office this summer. Election day is August 26th and we're hitting the ground running!

Come knock on doors of voters in the Alpharetta area as we look to engage voters ahead of the election. Canvassing is the best way to persuade voters to come to the polls for the August special election. No experience is necessary – just bring yourself, some comfortable walking shoes, water, sunscreen, and a charged cellphone. We will provide training, a script, and the addresses of targeted voters in the area. We'll also partner up volunteers who want to canvass with a group!

title: A Conversation with Rep. Sam McKenzie: Reflections from the Tennessee Legislature
description:
Join the Anderson County Democratic Women’s Club for a special evening with Tennessee State Representative Sam McKenzie on Monday, June 23 at 5:30 p.m. at 201 Café and Wine Bar, 201 Broadway Ave., Oak Ridge. Rep. McKenzie will offer insight into this year’s Tennessee General Assembly session, discuss legislative developments, and share his perspective as Chair of the Tennessee Black Caucus of State Legislators.

A veteran of both public service and scientific leadership, McKenzie represents Knoxville’s District 15 and serves on key committees including Education, Health, Government Operations, and House Ethics. He is a former Knox County Commissioner and retired leader from Oak Ridge National Laboratory, now running a small business in Knoxville.

This event is an opportunity to hear directly from one of Tennessee’s most engaged legislative voices. Light refreshments will be provided, and drinks will be available for purchase. All are welcome. For more information, contact the Democratic Women’s Club at ac-democratic-women@outlook.com.
